name: mc_survey
title: Survey terrain
description:
Surveys terrain over an x/z area: a colour heightmap image (height bands, water and lava in blue, relief shading, grid and contours) plus the numbers a picture cannot give: min/max/median height, surface materials and the largest flat zone with its coordinates and y.

WHEN TO USE: before a substantial build, to find a flat spot, water, and a sensible y level instead of guessing; to check terrain around the build area.
WHEN NOT TO USE: for a 3D read of placed blocks or underground structure (mc_inspect). Do not survey many tiny sub-areas when one call covers the site.

COORDINATES: X east, Z south. from/to are inclusive [x, z] pairs; area at most 200,000 cells (e.g. 300x300). Output heights are absolute y.
saveAs:"name" writes every column (first non-air block, and the ground below plants, trees and liquids, each with its y) to plugins/Ashlar/exports/<name>.json.gz for a script, and replies with the summary only: for terrain data over a large area, instead of decoding region files.

SIDE EFFECTS: read-only in the world (saveAs writes a file).

world.description: World name; default: the configured default world.

type.description: Surface to measure. SOLID: highest solid block (a river reads as its bed). SOLID_OR_LIQUID: includes liquid surfaces. SOLID_OR_LIQUID_NO_LEAVES (default): also ignores leaves (ground under a canopy). ANY: highest non-air block. TOP_SOLID_IGNORE_DECOR: the ground you would build on, stepping down through carpet, snow up to `snowLayers`, plants, torches, lanterns, rails, signs, buttons, pots and heads.

format.description: "image" (default). "text" gives an ASCII map instead; only when the user asks for one or images cannot be shown.

matrix.description: Append the per-block height matrix (about one token per cell). Default: off. Useful over a small area, e.g. to fill a hole to the surrounding height.

snowLayers.description: TOP_SOLID_IGNORE_DECOR only: snow up to this many layers (0-7) is looked through. Default 3.

walkHeight.description: Append the y a player's feet rest at on each column (65.5 on a bottom slab at 65, 65.063 on carpet, 66.5 on a fence). At most 4,096 columns.

saveAs.description: Export name ([a-z0-9_-], up to 64 characters): write the per-column file instead of the image, text map or matrix.

overwrite.description: saveAs only: replace an existing export of that name (default false).
